photo.caption: Front page of the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera on 11 November 1938: "Le leggi per la difesa della razza approvate dal Consiglio dei ministri" (English: "The laws for the defence of race approved by the Council of Ministers"). On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.
photo.description: Front page of Corriere della Sera the day Italian racial laws were enacted by the Fascist regime, in 1938.

photo.caption: Territories promised to Italy by the Treaty of London (1915): South Tyrol/Trentino-Alto Adige (tan), the Julian March and Dalmatia (tan), and the Snežnik Plateau area (green). After the end of World War I (1914–1918), Dalmatia was not assigned to Italy but to Yugoslavia.
